To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the data mining solution to the problem of non-paying customers of CLEC’s was not as successful as one hoped, but (2) a compromised but useful solution can still be found after understanding the actual needs of business, and (3) the probabilistic extension of randomized decision tree ensemble is a better method than single randomized decision tree for predicting the probability of default.

(1) the best method is a randomized decision tree ensemble method; (2) the best ensemble method is a probabilistic extension to Breiman’s random forests; (3) the best method for predicting posterior probabilities is a probabilistic ensemble method.

(1) cost-sensitive learning may not be possible if a cost-model cannot be defined; (2) a probabilistic model may be a better alternative to a binary model; (3) random decision tree ensemble methods are better than a single decision tree for probability estimation; and (4) the randomization of decision tree ensemble methods can help to avoid over-fitting and improve accuracy.

the success or failure of a data mining solution is often not determined by the technology, but by the ability of data mining practitioners and business analysts to work together to understand the business needs, and to make compromises between the business needs and technology solutions.
